newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cool to Rifkind initiative on Gulf tensions.
newsitem.headline: France cool to Rifkind initiative on Gulf tensions.

text.p: France on Tuesday reacted coolly to a British proposal to create an Organisation for Coooperation aimed at reducing conflict in the Middle East, saying the time was not ripe and similar bodies already existed.

British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind proposed in Abu Dhabi on Monday to set up a body on the lines of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to encourage regional cooperation and investment in the region.

"We share Malcolm Rifkind's view that the methodology of the OSCE could be useful in building confidence...but a system of this type would depend on a particular climate and on the achievement of significant progress in the peace process," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

Rifkind said the new organisation could include Turkey, and would eventually be open to countries like Iraq and Iran. He had already floated the idea with countries in the region and other allies like the United States, with a favourable response.
Senior officials travelling with Rifkind added that the idea was not designed to replace the Middle East peace process, but to prevent another such crisis erupting.
Rummelhardt, however, said other organisations with a similar purpose already existed and France was actively involved in supporting their activities.
